card.name: Heat-trapping power of greenhouse gases
card.fires_on: Words in climate text describing how a greenhouse gas such as methane or water vapor traps heat, including "heat", "-trapping", "trap", "potent" and the number in "20-times" or "25 times".

modes.label: Heat-trapping phrase
modes.description: Parts of the phrase "heat-trapping power" after a comparison of a gas's strength.
modes.example: a gas with 20-times the<< heat>>-trapping power

modes.label: Numbers in the comparison
modes.description: The multiplier number in "20-times" or "25 times" before heat-trapping power.
modes.example: contributing to climate change with 2<<5>> times the heat-trapping power of carbon

modes.label: Greenhouse gas description
modes.description: Words describing a gas as potent or able to trap thermal energy.
modes.example: levels of methane, a<< potent>> greenhouse gas.

card.plain: It lights up in climate passages about methane or water vapor trapping heat in the atmosphere.
